look_here_first: Look at adult leaf tips with a loupe: 3–5 broad distal lobes should show small AWNS/bristles (red-oak-group trait). Then check the conspicuous tawny-hairy, often 5-angled terminal buds (5–10 mm), glossy mature upper leaves, and dark bark broken into blocks. Do not rely on a 'duck-foot' leaf alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: deciduous red-oak-group tree, often small to medium sized on poor uplands

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf strongly obovate/obtrullate, narrow below and broad toward tip

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: usually 3–5 broad shallow lobes concentrated in distal half

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper surface dark glossy green; lower surface paler and often tawny-pubescent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature bark nearly black to dark gray, breaking into thick squarish blocks

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaf blade typically 70–200 mm long and 70–200 mm wide, strongly broader toward the tip; 3–5 broad shallow lobes and 3–10 awns/bristles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Upper surface mature glossy/glabrous; lower surface scurfy to scattered pubescent, not the densely yellowish glandular + stellate combination typical of post oak.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Terminal buds conic/narrowly ovoid, 5–10 mm long, noticeably 5-angled and tawny-pubescent; twigs about 2–4 mm wide, pubescent to tomentose.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Acorns mature in second year (biennial); turbinate cup about 6–10 mm high × 13–18 mm broad, enclosing about one-third of nut; scales often free/loose at rim.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Very dark mature bark in rectangular/irregular blocks; inner bark orangish (a nonessential feature and not a reason to damage a live tree).

key_traits.label: Oak training
key_traits.text: Use leaf architecture plus bark/twig/buds and mature acorn/cupule; never identify an oak from leaf silhouette alone.
